name: Installation Mode
shortDesc: Choose your setup path and archinstall profile context
detailedDesc: Mode 2 (Minimal) is the recommended clean canvas. Mode 1 is for post-install additions on top of an existing desktop. Mode 3 replaces a DE, and Mode 4 is tailored for ancient legacy hardware.

phase.title: Base & Architecture
phase.description: Core display server protocols, desktop architecture paradigms, and package manager helpers.

packages.name: Mode 2: Minimal Base + SimpleArch (Recommended)
packages.description: Official archinstall with the Minimal profile. SimpleArch manages GPU drivers, compositor, modular shell daemons, and baseline dotfiles without conflicts.
pros: Zero package collisions or pre-installed bloat
Complete control over GPU driver stack and Wayland engine
cons: Requires post-install script run on first reboot into Arch

packages.name: Mode 1: Desktop Profile Post-Install
packages.description: For systems where 'Desktop' (e.g. GNOME, KDE, or Hyprland) was chosen during archinstall. SimpleArch only adds ricing enhancements, dev tools, and utilities.
pros: Boot directly into a working desktop before running script
cons: May result in duplicate utilities (e.g. multiple terminals or launchers)

packages.name: Mode 3: Replace Existing Profile Choices
packages.description: Replaces an already installed desktop profile. Deactivates conflicting display managers and deploys the selected SimpleArch stack.
pros: Saves time compared to full disk re-partitioning and reinstallation
cons: Risk of leftover orphan config files
May require manual cleanup of old display managers

packages.name: Mode 4: Ancient Hardware Mode
packages.description: Tailored for legacy dual-core CPUs (Core 2 Duo / Pentium), non-Vulkan iGPUs, and low RAM (<=4GB). Recommends pure X11, lz4 zram, and lightweight tools.
pros: Smooth performance on 10-15 year old machines
cons: No Wayland features (touchpad gestures, fractional scaling)
